name: Notion
tagline: Create a Notion public connection and plug it into Composio. No review needed; Marketplace listing is optional.

cost.asStated: Free. A free Notion workspace is enough to create and test the connection.

steps.title: Create a public connection
instructions: Open the Notion Developer portal. In the Build section of the sidebar, select Public connections.
Click Create new connection.
Enter a connection name and pick the development workspace you'll test in.
Installation scope: pick Any workspace so any Notion user can connect.
Keep the form open. Redirect URIs and capabilities are on the same form (next step).

fields.label: Connection name
fields.hint: Shown to users on Notion's consent prompt

fields.label: Installation scope
fields.hint: Selected workspaces only limits installs to workspaces you pick now

warnings.text: Installation scope can't be changed after creation. Picking the wrong one means creating a new connection.
Selected workspaces only can't be listed on the Marketplace, and since Sep 1, 2026 it is subject to Free-plan block limits.
Older guides send you to notion.so/profile/integrations and call this a public integration. The docs now use the Developer portal.

steps.unconfirmed: Notion's docs list name, workspace, redirect URIs, scope and capabilities. We couldn't open the form logged out to see other required fields.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI and capabilities
instructions: Under OAuth Domain & URIs, add the Composio callback below as a redirect URI.
Under capabilities, tick only what your Notion tools need.
Read content to search and fetch; Update content to edit; Insert content to create pages.
Add Read comments / Insert comments only if your agent works with comments.
User capabilities: pick No user information unless a tool needs names or emails.
Create the connection.

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: HTTPS, exact match, no trailing slash

fields.label: Starter capabilities
fields.value: Read content, Update content, Insert content
fields.hint: Trim to what your tools use

warnings.text: Changing capabilities later makes every connected user re-authorize.
Notion has no OAuth scopes. Capabilities here plus the pages each user picks decide access.

problems.q: Connecting fails with a redirect URI error
a: The redirect URI under OAuth Domain & URIs doesn't match the one in your Composio auth config.
Paste the Composio callback exactly, with no trailing slash, and save.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret
instructions: Open your connection's Configuration tab.
Copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret.
Store the secret in a secret manager, never in git.
Ignore the Authorization URL field. Composio builds the sign-in URL from your client ID.

warnings.text: Notion says the Authorization URL field stays empty until the connection is submitted for review. Composio doesn't need it.
warnings.unconfirmed: We couldn't create a connection, so we didn't see whether the field is still empty before review.

a: Notion didn't accept the client ID and secret pair Composio sent.
Copy both again from the Configuration tab and update your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
instructions: Open the Notion toolkit in Composio and create an auth config.
Use the values below, then paste your OAuth client ID and client secret.
Leave scopes empty. Notion doesn't use them.
Save, then copy the auth config ID (ac_…) for the next step.

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Must match the redirect URI in Notion exactly

steps.unconfirmed: The link exists. We couldn't check, without logging in, whether it opens auth config creation directly. If not: Auth Configs → Create Auth Config.

problems.q: The link didn't open the Notion toolkit
a: Open Auth Configs in the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Pick Notion, choose OAuth2, and turn on your own developer credentials.

steps.title: Use the auth config in your agent
instructions: Pass the auth config ID when you create a session. Your coding agent can paste this in.
Toolkits you don't list keep using Composio's managed auth.

a: The session must include authConfigs with your ac_… ID for notion.
Toolkits not listed in authConfigs fall back to managed auth.

steps.title: Connect a test account
instructions: Start a connection for a test user and open the link.
Notion's prompt should show your connection name and capabilities, not Composio.
Click Select pages and pick the pages or databases the agent should use. Children are included.
Click Allow access. Pages are only shared once Composio finishes the token exchange.
Each Notion user connects separately. One user's connection doesn't cover teammates.
Users already connected through managed auth must reconnect.

warnings.text: The page picker only lists pages the user has full access to.
Every refresh returns a new refresh token too. Notion doesn't document how long access tokens last.
warnings.unconfirmed: Composio says it refreshes Notion tokens automatically. We didn't test a refresh end to end.

steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run a full connection. It needs a Composio API key and a real Notion sign-in.

problems.q: Tools return object_not_found or can't see my pages
a: The page wasn't shared during sign-in. Notion only exposes pages picked in the page picker.
On the page in Notion: ••• → More → Connections → Add connections, then pick your connection. Or reconnect and pick it.

problems.q: An older connection stopped working after the user reconnected
a: Reconnecting the same user to the same app can invalidate the older refresh token.
Keep one connection per user and reuse it. Delete the stale one.
The user clicked Cancel on Notion's prompt.
Start a new connection and have them click Select pages, then Allow access.

problems.q: The consent prompt still says Composio
a: The connection used the managed auth config. Pass your ac_… ID in the session.
Existing connections keep their old config. Delete and reconnect them.

steps.title: Get approved in Enterprise workspaces
steps.when: Only if a user's Enterprise workspace limits which connections members can install.
instructions: The user asks their workspace owner to approve your connection.
The owner installs your connection first. Only installed connections can be approved.
Then Settings → Connections → Manage → + Add approved connection, and pick yours.
Owner installs land on the approved list automatically.
After approval, the user connects with their own account.
steps.unconfirmed: We had no Enterprise workspace, so we didn't see the error a blocked member gets during OAuth.

problems.q: A user can't install the connection in their workspace
a: Their Enterprise workspace is set to Approved only or Approved & recommended.
A workspace owner must install it and add it to the approved list.

steps.title: List on the Notion Marketplace
steps.when: Only if you want Notion users to find you in the Marketplace. Not needed for OAuth to work.
instructions: Needs installation scope Any workspace.
Open the Marketplace listing dashboard → Listings → Connections → Start a new connection listing.
Add name, description, category, tags, images, logo, and pick your public connection.
Save the draft, then submit it for review from Listings → Connections.
Notion replies by email. If changes are needed, fix them and resubmit.

wait.asStated: Expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.

a: Notion emails the reason: brand or trademark issues, quality, or missing baseline criteria.
Fix what they list and resubmit from Listings → Connections.
